claims.explanation: AM-92016 is a delayed-rectifier potassium channel blocker with weak, non-selective pharmacology; its selective killing pattern is most plausibly explained by dependence on potassium-channel-driven membrane potential and calcium signaling, particularly in lines with high KCNH2/KCNQ1 expression or GRIN1/NMDA-receptor signaling that modulates survival under chronic blockade. The transcriptional similarity to calcium-channel and G-protein-coupled receptor antagonists suggests that cells with high calcium-channel or GPCR tone are more vulnerable, while efflux or survival-pathway upregulation protects.

features.basis: AM-92016 blocks delayed-rectifier K+ channels; high KCNH2 (hERG) expression increases dependence on this current for membrane potential and survival
Delayed-rectifier K+ channel family member; high expression predicts greater sensitivity to K+ channel blockade
Annotated target of AM-92016; NMDA-receptor signaling can promote survival, so blockade may selectively kill GRIN1-dependent lines
Transcriptional similarity to mibefradil (T-type calcium channel blocker) suggests shared dependence on T-type calcium channels
T-type calcium channel; high expression may increase vulnerability to calcium-signaling disruption by AM-92016
Small-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channel; high expression may compensate for delayed-rectifier blockade and support survival
BKCa channel; blockade exacerbates ischemic injury, so high expression may buffer against AM-92016 toxicity
Downregulated in the most responsive virtual-cell condition (HEPG2); high baseline expression may reflect a survival/anti-apoptotic state
Upregulated in the responsive HCC515 virtual-cell condition; TRIB1 supports proliferation and may mark dependence on signaling disrupted by AM-92016
GNA11 hotspot mutations drive constitutive Gq signaling; such lines may depend on calcium/K+ homeostasis and be more vulnerable to channel blockade
Upregulated in the responsive HEPG2 virtual-cell condition; PI3K pathway upregulation can confer survival signaling against drug-induced stress
Upregulated in the responsive HEPG2 virtual-cell condition; may mark a transcriptional state associated with sensitivity
